one_month_reasoning: The scheduled events inside the window are the FOMC on Oct 27-28 (Fed calendar) and T-Mobile's Q3 2026 report on Wednesday 2026-10-28 (release ~4:05pm ET, call 4:30pm ET; company release of 2026-09-17), so the stock reacts on Oct 29. Management already guided Q3 low on the Q2 call: ~250k postpaid account net adds (vs 396k in Q3 2025), service revenue ~$19.3B (+6%) and Core Adjusted EBITDA ~$9.4B (+8%), and the Sept 3 8-K reaffirmed 2026 guidance. So the swing factor is commentary rather than the print: whether the 2027 framework is restated in numbers, any early read on the 2027 return authorization, and the answer to SpaceX after the Grain deal that cut the stock 13.27% on Oct 9. Verizon and AT&T Q3 reports in late October (dates not confirmed by me) will also move the group. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways: reversal after an extreme one-day sector selloff, and continuation after news-driven drops at 52-week lows with negative momentum. I keep the round-1 ladder: almost symmetric around spot (median ~$149.5, a hair above $148.58 for ongoing buybacks and a pre-lowered bar) with a monthly sigma of ~10.5%, above the ~9.4% (33%/3.5) baseline because the window holds earnings and the FOMC and follows a volatility shock. Nothing the supervisor verified changes the one-month view, and I dropped the Alpha Vantage Q3 EPS consensus I cited in round 1 because it needs a key.

fair_value.method: Blend at the 2027-10-09 horizon, before ~$4.68 of dividends: (a) P/E 0.4 weight: 11.0x on horizon NTM EPS of $14.90 (FY2027 consensus $14.44 and FY2028 at +10%, weighted 25/75, less a 4% haircut) = $163.9; (b) EV/EBITDA 0.4 weight: 6.69x (company basis) on horizon-LTM Core Adjusted EBITDA of $38.95B, less $84.1B net debt and $3.46B towers, over ~1,015M horizon shares = $170.5; (c) FCF yield 0.2 weight: 12.0% on 2027 AFCF of $19.5B / 1,015M shares = $160.1. Blend 0.4 x 163.9 + 0.4 x 170.5 + 0.2 x 160.1 = $165.8, so $166.

inputs_detail.derivation: 14.44 x 1.10 = 15.88. +10% is below the 17.03% 3Y EPS growth forecast (src 13) because Q3 guidance slows service revenue to ~+6% and Core EBITDA to ~+8% (src 8) and 2027 consensus revenue growth is only +4.44% (src 12); buybacks of ~3-5% of shares a year carry most of the remaining EPS growth.

My 2027 Core EBITDA of $39.5B is 2.5% below the $40.5B midpoint of the target (src 4); with D&A and interest roughly fixed, that is about 4% at the EPS line. The SpaceX/Grain overhang (src 15, 27) mainly affects the multiple, not 2027 EPS, since SpaceX targets mobile service in H1 2028 (src 27). 15.52 x 0.96 = 14.90.

+16% vs the 9-peer median of 9.46x, inside the range and below TMUS's own 11.82x NTM P/E (src 13). Growth gap: TMUS 3Y EPS growth forecast 17.03% vs a peer median of 6.99% (src 13, 16-25); PEG 11.0/17.03 = 0.65 vs 9.46/6.99 = 1.35 for the peer median. Capped at about AMX's 10.9x (18.02% growth, src 23) because SpaceX and cable contest the growth premium. Down from 12.0x in round 1. methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 6.69x x horizon-LTM Core Adj. EBITDA $38.95B = EV $260.7B; less net debt $84.1B and towers $3.46B = equity $173.1B; / 1,015M shares = $170.5

inputs_detail.derivation: Midpoint of the Q2 guidance (src 1), reaffirmed on Sept 3 (src 6).

37.3 x 1.059 = 39.5. The company target is $40.0-41.0B (src 4), with the framework maintained on Sept 3 (src 6). Q3 is guided at ~+8% (src 8), but that still laps part of the UScellular acquisition, so I assume ~6% organic growth: 1.25% below the low end of the target.
0.25 x 37.3 + 0.75 x 39.5 = 9.33 + 29.63 = 38.95. The multiple is trailing, so it is applied to horizon-LTM EBITDA, not forward 2027 EBITDA (the supervisor's round-1 correction).

inputs_detail.input: Net debt excl. tower obligations (Jun 30 2026), held flat to the horizon
inputs_detail.derivation: Held flat: AFCF of roughly $9B in H2 2026 (2026 guide $18.4-18.8B, src 1) plus ~$14.6B for 0.75 of 2027 (low end $19.5B, src 4) exceeds the ~$17B of returns the $30B envelope allows over the period (src 1, 4). The surplus is assumed to go to spectrum (the 2027-28 envelope flagged on the Q2 call, src 8), not debt paydown.

Start: 1,072.7M on Jul 17 2026 (src 3). Remaining 2026 authorization: $18.2B (src 1) less H1 buybacks $7.15B (src 3 cash flow), H1 dividends ~$2.2B (Q2 $1.1B, src 1; Q1 ~1.02 x ~1.10B shares) and $0.39B bought to Jul 17 (src 1) = ~$8.4B. Less the Sept dividend (1.02 x 1.073B = $1.09B) and the Dec dividend (1.17 x ~1.06B = $1.24B, src 26) = ~$6.1B of buybacks at ~$165 = ~37M shares. 2027: up to ~$30B of returns through 2027 (src 4) less $18.2B = $11.8B; less ~$4.8B of dividends (4 x 1.17 x ~1.03B) = ~$7.0B; 0.75 by October = $5.2B at ~$155 = ~34M shares. Issuance: 3.45M shares per half-year in H1 2026 (ESPP 0.75M + RSUs 2.70M, src 3) x 2.5 = ~8.6M. 1,072.7 - 37 - 34 + 8.6 = 1,010M, rounded up to 1,015M in case 2027 buybacks are pared for spectrum.

bear.story: Starlink Mobile gains credibility: a fast FCC approval of the Grain 800 MHz transfer, an MVNO or roaming deal with a rival, or aggressive pre-launch pricing. On top of that, a Verizon/AT&T/cable promotional war, account adds below the 950k-1.05M 2026 guide, and a 2027 framework cut by ~10%. Horizon NTM EPS ~13% below the $15.52 consensus-based path (~$13.5) at a Verizon-like 8.25x = ~$111, so ~$112.

base.story: Rate-plan churn fades after Q3. 2026 guidance is met, and 2027 lands slightly below the low end (~$39.5B Core EBITDA, ~$19.5B AFCF). Buybacks under the ~$30B envelope take the count to ~1,015M. SpaceX stays a 2028 issue (its CFO targets H1 2028) but holds the multiple near 10.75x the haircut horizon NTM EPS of $14.90 = ~$160, plus ~$4.68 of dividends.

bull.story: Q3/Q4 show churn normalising and account adds back above 250k a quarter. The 2027 targets are restated or beaten, and a large 2027 return authorization at depressed prices is announced. The FCC process or a carrier response defuses the SpaceX threat. The stock re-rates to ~12.5x the unhaircut horizon NTM EPS of $15.52 = ~$194, near the summer-2026 trading range.

comps_summary.peer_range: 9 peers (VZ, T, CMCSA, RCI, TU, BCE, AMX, VOD, TIMB), all re-opened on StockAnalysis at the 2026-10-09 close. Forward P/E 5.90x (CMCSA) to 15.46x (TU); trailing EV/EBITDA (lease-inclusive EV) 4.58x (CMCSA) to 9.72x (TU); FCF yield 10.63% (BCE) to 29.23% (VOD), median 13.68%. Excluded: CHTR (distressed outlier at 2.34x forward P/E on a $16.91B market cap, src 19) and DTE (it consolidates TMUS, so circular). Fewer than 10 because no other listed carrier is a genuine comparable without being distressed or circular.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: TMUS today: 11.82x NTM P/E, 10.29x FY2027 consensus ($148.58/$14.44), 8.06x trailing EV/EBITDA on the peer basis (6.88x on mine), 11.54% FCF yield. Chosen: 11.0x P/E (+16% vs the 9.46x median), 6.69x EV/EBITDA on my basis (7.84x on the peer basis, +10%), and a 12.0% FCF yield (vs a 13.68% median). All are inside the peer ranges, and all are at or below TMUS's current multiples on NTM/trailing figures.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The premium rests on reported, structural growth gaps, not on sell-side outperformance calls. (1) The 3Y EPS growth forecast is 17.03% vs a 6.99% peer median (VZ 6.99%, T 11.06%); PEG at 11x is 0.65 vs 1.35 for the peer median. (2) Reported growth: Q2 2026 service revenue +8.9% and Core Adjusted EBITDA +11.7%; 2027 targets of $40-41B Core EBITDA and $19.5-20.5B AFCF maintained on Sept 3. (3) Buybacks shrink the share count 3-5% a year at 2.3x leverage vs a 2.5x target. The premium is held to ~10-16%, versus 23-27% in round 1, because: SpaceX and cable contest exactly this growth; AMX trades at 10.9x on 18% growth; part of the EPS growth is buybacks; and account adds are decelerating (Q3 guide ~250k) while postpaid phone net adds are no longer disclosed. I keep TIMB in the set (re-verified) where the supervisor dropped it; with its 8-peer set the median would be 9.95x, and 11.0x would be +10.6%.

thesis_break_reason: $115 is about 8.0x the verified FY2027 consensus EPS of $14.44, below Verizon's 8.23x forward P/E even though TMUS's 3Y EPS growth forecast (17.03%) is more than twice Verizon's (6.99%). It is also ~16% FCF yield on the low end of 2027 AFCF guidance ($19.5B / 1,072.7M shares = $18.18). A sustained trade there would most likely mean the growth premise had broken, not ordinary volatility (~23% below spot, about 0.8 sigma at 30% vol, after a 13% one-day drop). Likely causes: the 2027 framework withdrawn or cut, a structural price war (account adds below ~200k a quarter, ARPA growth turning negative), or SpaceX securing nationwide wholesale access or an MVNO and a launch date before 2028.

catalysts.event: FOMC decision (Oct 27-28); rates matter for a leveraged dividend payer
Q3 2026 results (after close) and call: ~250k account adds guided; watch the 2027 framework wording, Q4 churn normalisation and the SpaceX response
Verizon and AT&T Q3 results: read-across on switching, promotions and pricing (dates not confirmed by me)
Ex-dividend for the raised $1.17 quarterly dividend (paid Dec 10)
FCC review of the SpaceX purchase of Grain's 800 MHz licenses; SpaceX targets mobile service in H1 2028
Board authorization of the 2027 shareholder return program (the 2026 one was announced 2025-12-11; the envelope is up to ~$30B of returns for 2026-27, so ~$11.8B is left for 2027 unless raised)
Q4 2026 results and 2027 guidance; Jessica Uhl becomes CFO
Possible upper C-band / 2.7 GHz spectrum spending that management said is reserved in the 2027-28 capital envelope, which may crowd out buybacks
Q1 and Q2 2027 results: progress toward the 2027 targets; CFO Osvaldik retires July 1 2027

key_uncertainties: How credible and how fast SpaceX/Starlink Mobile is as a fourth carrier. The Grain deal needs FCC approval, and SpaceX's CFO targets satellite mobile service in H1 2028 while staying undecided on a terrestrial network. That puts most of the P&L effect after the horizon, but the multiple bears it now.

Whether the 2027 targets ($40-41B Core EBITDA, $19.5-20.5B AFCF) survive. They were maintained on Sept 3 but not restated as numbers at the September conferences; my base case sits 1.25% below the EBITDA low end.
Account growth is decelerating (Q3 guide ~250k vs 396k a year earlier) and postpaid phone net adds are no longer disclosed.
The horizon share count depends on whether the board raises the ~$30B 2026-27 return envelope or diverts cash to spectrum: 1,015M is my estimate, and each 20M shares is ~$3 a share.
The sector-wide de-rating and the rate backdrop. Peer multiples may compress further regardless of TMUS execution.
The size of any contingent payment from Grain's resale to SpaceX is not disclosed as a formula, so it is excluded from value.
Management transition: a new CFO from Feb 2027, a new Chief Enterprise Officer and the departure of the product chief.
reasoning: Round 2. I accepted the supervisor's evidence-backed corrections after re-checking them at source, and kept my own judgment elsewhere. Re-verified: the FY2027 consensus EPS of $14.44 (StockAnalysis forecast, explicitly 'non-GAAP adjusted', the same basis as the forward P/Es), which replaces the keyed Alpha Vantage $13.94, now removed from every number and from my sources; the Feb 2026 outlook 8-K wording ('$40.0-$41.0 billion in 2027', AFCF '$19.5-$20.5 billion in 2027', 'up to approximately $30 billion for stockholder returns' in the envelope through 2027); the $18.2B 2026 return authorization, $0.39B bought to Jul 17, and H1 buybacks of 34.75M shares for $7.1B (Q2 release, 10-Q); the dividend raise to $1.17 for December (StockAnalysis); all peer multiples; SpaceX's H1 2028 target (Light Reading); and the FOMC on Oct 27-28. I could not open the 10-Q's Note 12 (the fetch truncates), so I derive the ~$8.4B remaining authorization from the release and cash-flow figures instead of citing $8.5B. Changes to methods: (1) the P/E now uses $14.44 and a horizon NTM EPS of $14.90 after a 4% haircut, at 11.0x instead of 12.0x; the +23-27% premium was not defensible while SpaceX contests the growth and AMX trades 10.9x on 18% growth. (2) EV/EBITDA now applies a trailing multiple to horizon-LTM EBITDA ($38.95B), not forward 2027 EBITDA, and divides by ~1,015M horizon shares rather than today's 1,072.7M; my 2027 EBITDA is $39.5B, between my round-1 $40.0B and the supervisor's $39.0B. (3) I added an FCF-yield leg on the 2027 AFCF low end. Where I disagree with the supervisor: I hold net debt flat at $84.1B rather than letting it grow at 2.3x leverage, because the capped return envelope (~$17B over the period) is below the ~$23-24B of AFCF, so extra borrowing is not needed to fund the buybacks I count; and I keep TIMB in the peer set (median 9.46x rather than 9.95x). Fair value moves from $169 to $166. Distribution: unchanged logic. A new-entrant narrative and a sector de-rating usually cap multiples for a while, and 12-month momentum is -34%, so I centre the 12-month median at ~$154 (spot plus about a third of the gap to fair value), consistent with a 25/50/25 bear/base/bull of $112/$160/$195 (probability-weighted ~$157), sigma ~30% (realised 33%) and a slightly fat left tail. The upper strikes are trimmed by 0.5-1 point for the lower multiple cap. The thesis break moves to $115, 8.0x verified FY2027 EPS. Lane: 11 of 28 sources are in-lane primary documents; the gap to 60% comes from the 10 per-peer data pages the comp table requires plus the consensus and dividend data pages. No option prices or implied volatility were consulted.
